stem: How can accessibility practices such as alternative text, headings, and transcripts benefit search engine optimization (SEO)?

options.text: Search engines give higher rankings to pages that publish an accessibility statement or badge.
options.rationale: An accessibility statement documents conformance for users; search engines do not treat it as a ranking factor.

options.text: Crawlers require a passing automated WCAG conformance audit before they will index a page.
options.rationale: Search engines index pages whether or not they meet WCAG; conformance is a W3C standard, not a crawler requirement.

options.text: Crawlers rank pages by counting the number of ARIA attributes in the markup.
options.rationale: ARIA attributes describe semantics to assistive technology; crawlers do not rank pages by counting them.

options.text: They turn visual and multimedia content into text that crawlers can read and index.
options.rationale: Alternative text, headings, and transcripts give search engines readable text for content that images and media would otherwise hide.

explanation: Search engines index text. Alternative text, headings, and transcripts present the same content in a form that crawlers can read, so what makes a page accessible to assistive technology also makes it discoverable in search.

references.title: Google Search Central: SEO Starter Guide
